thread:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a slow steady memory growth in the KV residency counters on prod-gpu-04 over the last 36h. Tenant cluster T-42 shows rising pagewalks and never-evicted longctx entries.

maria: Hmm. Any perf regressions or latency spikes tied to that?

alex: p95 token latency stable but p99 increased ~120ms for requests that hit large context prefixes. Also observed higher swap/page faults on the node. Quick profiler snippet: 
```
pprof -proto cpu.pb /srv/inference/bin/runtime 
# top: kv_pagewalk (38%)
#   kv_reclaim_scan (21%)
#   kv_lookup (12%)
```

sam: Can you paste the KV residency dump? Is it mostly fragmentation (many small pages pinned) or a few oversized allocations?

alex: Dump: 
```
RESIDENCY SUMMARY:
 total_pages=248k
 tenant_T-42=98k (peak 116k 48h ago)
 free_fragments=12k (avg size 128B)
 longctx_entries=17k (avg age 4.1h)
 evicted_since_restart=3.2k
```

tess: That reads like fragmentation + stale longctx retention. We've seen the allocator fail to coalesce after repeated KV reuse patterns from streaming chat. Those small fragments block new full-page allocations.

maria: Repro steps? I can spin a repro rig if you give the sequence.

alex: Repro command: 
```bash
# spawn 50 simulated users streaming longctx (seq len 8k -> 32k)
./scripts/loadgen --tenants T-42 --streams 50 --pattern longctx-burst --duration 2h --kv-prefetch=on
```
observed when prefetch and continuous-batching enabled together.

sam: Sounds like a heuristics miscoord: prefetch pins more partial KVs, batching keeps KV cache warm, and eviction doesn't consider fragmentation. Two options: 1) tighten per-tenant resident watermarks so eviction triggers earlier; 2) add compaction pass to coalesce small fragments during low load.

tess: We also found a bug where page-age watermark used wall-clock instead of request-count — so longctx entries never crossed the eviction age threshold under bursty traffic. Patch queued: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/+/fix/kv-age.

jin: +1 for adding a lightweight compaction in the background. But be careful: compaction = copying pages -> CPU + GPU memory pressure. Maybe run it only when free_fragments > threshold AND node idle_cpu_pct > 40.

alex: Agree. Also want to test switching the eviction policy from LRU to an age+size hybrid for longctx-heavy tenants. Sam, can you prototype a weighted-evict heuristic?

sam: I'll sketch it. Idea: score = alpha*age_score + beta*(page_size_norm) + gamma*(tenant_penalty). For noisy tenants we up tenant_penalty so they shed residency faster. Will push a prototype to my branch.

maria: If we change tenant_penalty we need a rollout plan for Dedicated customers — risk of latencies spike during rebalancing. Can we do canary with reshuffle window and soft-evict (notify + allow grace period)?

tess: We already have soft-evict flags in rollout. Suggest: 1) canary on non-SLA cluster 2) enable compaction background job 3) switch heuristic with soft-evict for 24h then hard-enforce.

infra-bot: deploy job queued: runtime/kv/compaction-job v0.1 -> staging (ci-789)

alex: Next actions:
- Sam: prototype weighted-evict branch + unit tests (ETA 48h)
- Tess: land kv-age fix + add fragment threshold check for compaction (ETA 24h)
- Maria: run repro loadgen w/ patch once staging build available and collect p99/p95 over 6h windows (ETA after staging deploy)
- Jin: add node-level compaction gating based on cpu% (I'll open infra ticket)

maria: One more ask — please add a lightweight perf counter in the runtime metrics for "fragment_coalesce_ops" and "longctx_pin_count" so we can alert before p99 drift.

alex: Good call. I'll add those metrics to the telemetry PR.

sam: I'll also add a small sim harness to emulate skewed multi-tenant mixes so we can test fair-penalty effects before canarying.

tess: Thanks team, keeping this thread as the single source for rollout notes. Will update when fixes land. :white_check_mark:
